name: Jerusalem
line: Jerusalem is a mountain city, also called the city of David and the holy city, where God's temple stood and where the Bible's kings, prophets, and Jesus all came.

moments.title: David plans for the temple
moments.text: David called Israel's leaders to Jerusalem. He told them God had chosen his son Solomon, not David, to build the house for God's Name.

moments.title: The LORD saves Jerusalem
moments.text: The Assyrians shouted against the God of Jerusalem. Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed, and the LORD sent an angel, saved the people, and gave them rest on every side.

moments.title: Ezra arrives safely
moments.text: Ezra and the people set out for Jerusalem, and the hand of God protected them from enemies and bandits on the way. They arrived and rested there for three days.

moments.title: Jesus visits the pool
moments.text: Jesus went up to Jerusalem for a feast. Near the Sheep Gate, at the pool called Bethesda, He saw a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years and told him to get up and walk.

name: Egypt
line: Egypt is the land of the Nile, where Abram fled a famine and Jacob's family settled, and from which God later brought Israel out.

moments.title: Abram goes down to Egypt
moments.text: A severe famine hit the land, so Abram went to Egypt for a while. He asked Sarai to say she was his sister, afraid the Egyptians would kill him for her.

moments.title: Jacob's family comes to Egypt
moments.text: Jacob's family came to Egypt, including two sons born to Joseph there. In all, seventy members of the family went to Egypt.

moments.title: The Nile turns to blood
moments.text: The fish in the Nile died and the river smelled so bad the Egyptians could not drink it. Egypt's magicians did the same, and Pharaoh's heart stayed hard.

moments.title: Isaiah's sign against Egypt
moments.text: The LORD had Isaiah go naked and barefoot for three years as a sign against Egypt and Cush. The king of Assyria would lead Egypt's captives away, and those who boasted in Egypt would be ashamed.

moments.title: A blessing for Egypt
moments.text: The LORD promised a day when Egypt and Assyria would worship together and join Israel in a blessing on the earth. He called Egypt "My people."

name: Lebanon
line: Lebanon is a mountain region north of Israel, famous for its tall cedar trees, and the Bible names it as promised land and a source of building wood.

moments.title: Part of the promised land
moments.text: At Horeb, God tells Israel to go and take the land He promised, reaching to Lebanon and the great River Euphrates.

moments.title: God's promise for Lebanon
moments.text: God tells Joshua that land is still left to take, including all Lebanon to the east. He promises that He Himself will drive out the people of the Lebanon hill country before Israel.

moments.title: Wood from Lebanon for the temple
moments.text: Solomon sends word that he wants cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon. He says the king's servants are skilled at cutting timber there.

moments.title: Logs for the second temple
moments.text: After the exile, the people give food, drink, and oil to workers from Sidon and Tyre, who bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. Cyrus king of Persia had given his permission.

moments.title: A prophecy about proud cedars
moments.text: Isaiah says a day is coming when the LORD will come against everything proud, including the tall cedars of Lebanon. On that day only the LORD will be lifted up.

name: Tarshish
line: Tarshish was a far-off place across the sea, known for its ships and rich cargo, and it is where Jonah tried to run when he fled from the LORD.

moments.title: Kings of Tarshish bring tribute
moments.text: A prayer for the king asks that the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute. It puts Tarshish among the far places whose rulers bring gifts.

moments.title: Wail, ships of Tarshish
moments.text: Isaiah speaks against Tyre and calls on the ships of Tarshish to wail, because Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor.

moments.title: Daughter of Tarshish
moments.text: Isaiah spoke against Tyre and called to the Daughter of Tarshish. He said there was no longer a harbor.

moments.title: Silver from Tarshish
moments.text: Jeremiah says hammered silver is brought from Tarshish. A craftsman works it into idols, but the LORD is the true God.

moments.title: Ships of Tarshish carry cargo
moments.text: Ezekiel says the ships of Tarshish carried Tyre's merchandise. Tyre was filled with heavy cargo in the heart of the sea.

name: Tarsus
line: Tarsus was a well-known city in Cilicia and the hometown of Saul, who became the apostle Paul, and it is where he was sent and later sought out.

moments.title: Ananias asks for a man from Tarsus
moments.text: The Lord tells Ananias to go to Judas' house on Straight Street in Damascus. There he is to ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, who is praying.

moments.title: Barnabas looks for Saul
moments.text: Barnabas goes to Tarsus to look for Saul. When he finds him, he brings him back to Antioch, and they teach large numbers of people there.

moments.title: Paul names his hometown
moments.text: Paul tells a crowd he is a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. He then asks to speak to the people, and tells them he was born in Tarsus.

name: Jabbok
line: The Jabbok is a stream east of the Jordan River where Jacob wrestled and was renamed Israel, and later a border mark for Israel and the Ammonites.

moments.title: Jacob crosses the river
moments.text: During the night Jacob took his two wives, his two servant women, and his eleven sons and crossed the shallow crossing place of the Jabbok. He sent them across the stream with all his things.

moments.title: Israel's land reaches the Jabbok
moments.text: After Israel defeated Sihon, they took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok. They went no farther than the border of the Ammonites, because their land was protected by strong walls.

moments.title: Land along the Jabbok left alone
moments.text: Moses reminded Israel that they did not go near the land along the banks of the Jabbok River. The LORD had forbidden it.

moments.title: The Jabbok marks the border
moments.text: Moses gave the Reubenites and Gadites land from Gilead to the Arnon Valley and up to the Jabbok River. The Jabbok was the border of the Ammonites.

moments.title: Jephthah answers the Ammonites
moments.text: The Ammonite king said Israel had taken his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok. Jephthah replied that the LORD had driven out the Amorites and given the land to Israel.
